words.gloss: vyoṣa (a set of three drugs: dry ginger, long pepper, black pepper; standard); trijātaka (a set of three: cinnamon bark, small cardamom, Indian bay leaf; standard); ambhoda (probably musta, nut-grass; lit. 'water-giver'); kṛmighna (probably vidanga, Embelia ribes; lit. 'worm-slayer'); āmalaka (Indian gooseberry, Phyllanthus emblica; standard)

hindi: व्योष यानी सोंठ पीपर और काली मिर्च, त्रिजातक यानी दालचीनी इलायची और तेजपात, अम्भोद यानी प्रायः नागरमोथा, कृमिघ्न यानी प्रायः वायविडंग और आमलक यानी आँवला के साथ त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ
english: Trivṛt (turpeth) together with vyoṣa (the set of three: dry ginger, long pepper, black pepper), trijātaka (the set of three: cinnamon bark, small cardamom, Indian bay leaf), ambhoda (probably musta, nut-grass), kṛmighna (probably vidanga) and āmalaka (Indian gooseberry).
notes: GROUPING: 38 and 39 form one sentence (38 names the ingredients; 39 gives the proportion and the pills). The unit is one printed line without a space. Identifications (modern names beside the Sanskrit): trivṛt = turpeth, Operculina turpethum (standard). vyoṣa = śuṇṭhī (dry ginger, Zingiber officinale), pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum), marica (black pepper, Piper nigrum) (standard group). trijātaka = tvak (cinnamon bark, Cinnamomum zeylanicum), elā (small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum), patra (Indian bay leaf, Cinnamomum tamala) (standard group). ambhoda = musta, nut-grass, Cyperus rotundus (probable; ambhoda is a synonym of musta). kṛmighna = vidanga, Embelia ribes (probable; 'worm-slayer' is a synonym of vidanga). āmalaka = Indian gooseberry, Phyllanthus emblica (standard). Case of trivṛt (nom.) and of the instrumental compound is read from the form.

english: Equal to all of them, with an equal amount of sugar, pills are made with honey.
notes: GROUPING: continues 38. 'samā' is taken with trivṛt of 38 ('equal to all [the others]'); samasitā read as 'having equal sugar'. Verb 'kṛtāḥ' is 'are made' (participle, no copula).

english: In mūtrakṛcchra (urine-difficulty: painful or difficult urination, dysuria), fever, vomiting and cough; in wasting (śoṣa, a consumption-like wasting), giddiness (bhrama, vertigo) and decay (kṣaya, wasting).
notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 41 (verb 'śastāḥ'). Sandhi: 'jvaracchardi' = jvara-chardi. 'mūtrakṛcchra' may be one disease-term (urine-difficulty) rather than two members. Modern equivalents beside the Sanskrit terms: mūtrakṛcchra = painful or difficult urination (dysuria; standard); jvara = fever; chardi = vomiting; kāsa = cough; bhrama = giddiness, vertigo (standard); śoṣa = wasting, commonly equated with consumption (probable); kṣaya = wasting, sometimes the disease rājayakṣmā (disputed here).

english: In thirst, in pāṇḍu-ailment (pāṇḍu disease: anaemia with pallor), when the fire (agni) is small (weak digestion), and in all poisons, they are approved.

english: Having prepared a powder, it is to be saturated for seven days in the juice from āmalaka (Indian gooseberry).
notes: 'āmalakād rase' is an ablative + locative ('in the juice from āmalaka'); a genitive ('āmalakasya') would be expected, so the reading is slightly uncertain. 'bhāvya' rendered 'to be saturated' (OPEN verb wording).

hindi: वह तर्पण में, यूष में, मांस में और रागयुक्तियों में प्रयोग करने योग्य है।
english: That is to be used in tarpaṇa (a satiating drink), in broth (yūṣa), in meat, and in rāga-preparations.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tayojyaṃ' is not a word; 'tad yojyam' ('that is to be joined') fits the metre; 'prayojyaṃ' is another possibility

notes: 'rāgayukti' = preparations with rāga (flavouring/colouring); sense taken literally and not firm. tarpaṇa and yūṣa kept as technical terms with plain glosses.

hindi: बराबर खट्टे द्रव के साथ, त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ के कल्क से सिद्ध किया हुआ घृत गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ को हरने वाला है।
english: Ghee (ghṛta) cooked with a paste of trivṛt (turpeth), with an equal amount of sour liquid, takes away gulma (abdominal lump).
notes: 'tulyāmla' read as 'equal [measure of] sour liquid'; the thing it is equal to is not stated. 'siddha' here is 'cooked'.

hindi: श्यामा और त्रिवृत् के काढ़े से सिद्ध किया हुआ घृत, अथवा दूध भी।
english: Ghee cooked with a decoction of śyāmā and trivṛt (turpeth), or milk also.
notes: 'kaṣāya' rendered 'decoction' (glossary OPEN: kaṣāya/kvātha/niryūha kept as the same word so far). 'payaḥ' is read as milk cooked in the same way.

hindi: त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ की नखसहित आठ मुट्ठियाँ एक द्रोण जल में पकाए।
english: One should boil eight handfuls of trivṛt (turpeth), with nails, in a droṇa of water.
notes: 'sanakhān' (with nails) is kept literal; it appears to be a measure of handful, meaning not explained here. droṇa is a measure of volume.

hindi: एक चौथाई शेष रहा हुआ, छाना हुआ वह काढ़ा, एक तुला गुड़ से युक्त
english: That decoction, with a quarter remaining, strained, joined with a tulā of jaggery.
notes: GROUPING: sentence continues in 66. 'tulā' is a unit of weight (lit. 'balance'). 'kaṣāya' rendered 'decoction'.

hindi: चिकने घड़े में शहद, पिप्पली यानी पीपर के फल और चित्रक यानी चीता के साथ रखना चाहिए।
english: It is to be placed in a greased pot, with honey, the fruit of pippalī (long pepper) and citraka (leadwort).
notes: 'pippalī-phala' read as 'fruit of pippalī' (alternative: separate items). 'with' means mixed in.

words.gloss: pale (pāṇḍu; as a disease name, anaemia with pallor); swelling; gulma (abdominal lump); conquering

hindi: लेप किए जाने पर, एक मास बीत जाने पर, पीया हुआ यह पाण्डु यानी रक्ताल्पता, शोथ यानी सूजन और गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ को जीतने वाला है।
english: When it is smeared and a month has passed, drunk, it conquers pāṇḍu (anaemia), swelling and gulma (abdominal lump).
notes: 'lipte' is read as the pot being smeared/sealed (not stated). 'pāṇḍu' kept as 'pale' (glossary), here a condition-name. 'śvayathu' = swelling.

words.gloss: trivṛt; a quarter; ferment (kiṇva) (conjectural reading of damaged 'pādārkiṇvā')
words.gram: compound type uncertain, f. nom. sg. (conjectural)

hindi: अथवा सुरा, उसके क्वाथ से युक्त; मुद्रित समास 'त्रिवृतापादार्किण्वा' बिगड़ा हुआ है, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार वह त्रिवृत् के पादांश के किण्व वाली है।
english: Or a surā (spirituous drink) joined with its decoction; the printed compound 'trivṛtāpādārkiṇvā' is damaged, and on a conjectural reading it describes the surā as having a ferment (kiṇva) of a quarter of trivṛt.

text_flags.why: possible: stray 'r'; the compound is not clear in print

notes: Compound is doubtful: the printed 'pādārkiṇvā' is not clear; 'pāda-kiṇvā' ('a quarter [of trivṛt]' with 'ferment') is a guess. 'kvātha' rendered 'decoction'. Hindi keeps क्वाथ.

words.gloss: with yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare; standard) grains

hindi: श्यामा और त्रिवृत् के क्वाथ में स्वेदित यव यानी जौ के दानों से, जल के साथ कुल्माष
english: Kulmāṣa with barley grains steamed in a decoction of śyāmā and trivṛt, with water.
notes: GROUPING: probably continues in 70. 'kulmāṣa' kept as a name. 'svinna' = sweated/steamed.

words.gloss: sauvīraka (a sour fermented drink, here from barley; standard)

hindi: छह दिन भिगोया हुआ, पक जाने पर बना हुआ सौवीरक यानी खट्टा किण्वित पेय पिए।
english: Steeped for six days, when ripened, the sauvīraka (a sour fermented barley drink) that has arisen one should drink.
notes: GROUPING: 69, 70 and 71-72 form one linked passage (kulmāṣa/barley preparations). Exact connection of 'āsutam' and 'jātam' to the noun is not clear; 'sauvīraka' kept as a name.
lines_deva: आसुतं षडहं पक्के जातं सौवीरकं पिबेत्
lines_iast: āsutaṃ ṣaḍahaṃ pakke jātaṃ sauvīrakaṃ pibet

hindi: भुने हुए अथवा तुष सहित सूखे यव यानी जौ, उसके चूर्ण से युक्त
english: Roasted, or dry barley grains with husk, joined with its powder.

text_flags.why: possible: 'yāvāṃs' for 'yavāṃs' (yavān); the book may also mean a different form

notes: This line is printed as two tokens only (no spaces inside the long second token). GROUPING: continues in 72. 'tat' = that powder (of trivṛt, as before). Reviewer: 'saṃyuktam' (n. sg.) does not agree with masculine plural 'yavān'; possibly saṃyuktān, or the phrase is an independent apposition. Sense unchanged.

hindi: जल के साथ भिगोए हुओं को, उसी प्रकार बना हुआ तुषोदक पिए।
english: Steeped with water, likewise one should drink the husk-water that has arisen.

text_flags.why: typo: 'tupa' for 'tuṣa' (husk); 'tuṣodaka' is a known drink name

notes: Continues 71. 'tuṣodaka' = husk-water (literal). The printed tokens are 3 (the second is a run-together phrase).

words.gloss: heart; ailment (hṛdroga: heart disease); Vāta; blood (vātāsṛj; if read as one term, vātarakta, a gout-like disease; probable); udāvarta (upward turning: reversed movement of Vāta with retention of stool and wind); and so on; those who have an ailment

hindi: ज्वर यानी बुखार, हृद्रोग यानी हृदय रोग, वातासृक् यानी प्रायः वातरक्त, उदावर्त यानी वायु की उलटी गति से होने वाला रोग आदि रोग वालों में
english: In those afflicted with fever, heart-ailment (heart disease), Vāta-blood (perhaps vātarakta, a gout-like disease), udāvarta (reversed movement of Vāta, with retention of stool and wind) and the like.

text_flags.why: possible: stray space; 'jvara' belongs to the compound (jvara-hṛdroga-…)

notes: GROUPING: this verse is the end of the passage; its verb is in an earlier unit. 'vātāsṛj' may be one term (Vāta-blood) or 'Vāta and blood' (two). 'udāvarta' kept in Sanskrit (lit. 'upward turning').

words.gloss: rājavṛkṣa (golden shower tree, Cassia fistula, i.e. āragvadha; standard; lit. 'king-tree')

hindi: राजवृक्ष यानी अमलतास विशेष रूप से पथ्य, मृदु, मधुर और शीतल है।
english: Rājavṛkṣa (golden shower tree) is especially suitable, mild, sweet and cool.
notes: 'pathya' rendered 'suitable' (lit. 'fit for the way'). Rājavṛkṣa = golden shower tree, Cassia fistula, i.e. āragvadha (standard; Hindi amaltas). This verse may start a new topic (GROUPING: 73-74 probably separate sentences).
